Green Arrow’s “superpower” is his extraordinary archery skills—he is a master archer and marksman, able to hit targets with pinpoint accuracy and use a variety of specialized arrows.

An Indiegogo fundraising campaign asking for $200,000 was launched on March 23 and reached $2.4 million by April 24.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-Indiegogo-3) Fundraising closed with $3.4 million on December 31, 2019, with the continued campaign helping recover costs of DVD pressings and the distribution to contributors of perks, wardrobe, and props from the production.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-Indiegogo-3) A four-minute segment of the film's closing credits shows a list of only some of the 30,810 contributors[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-Indiegogo-3) to the fundraising campaign.
The first announcement of additional cast came on June 12, 2017, when Laysla De Oliveira joined.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-4)
Principal photography began on June 1, 2017, in Toronto.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-5)

Stephen Amell, star of the upcoming “Baywatch” reboot, first came to public attention as Oliver Queen in DC superhero series “Arrow.” But the actor says his new role isn’t so different.
“Once I got on it and I put on the red trunks, I realized, like, why does this feel so familiar?” Amell said of working on “Baywatch.” “It’s because it’s a superhero show. That’s what it feels like to me, and that makes my job easy.”
